Docs site

How the gatefox.dev docs site is built from docs/ and published to GitHub Pages.

About 4 min read · 2 sections

On this page
01 Search and sharing 02 Hosting

scripts/build-docs-site.mjs builds the site into .state/docs-site. It copies the hand-written guide (docs/index.html, styles.css, app.js, assets/), renders every docs/*.md page to HTML with marked (MIT, build-time only), and writes reference.html, a grouped list of every page built from its front matter. A page missing from every group appears under "More", so none is dropped. Links between docs become site pages; links to other repository files go to GitHub.

The landing page shows the latest complete, published app release, its date, versioned download and release notes. changelog.html lists published app releases and links to the full source changelog. Drafts, prereleases and incomplete assets never become download candidates. Versions in package.json and Unreleased notes do not imply that an app shipped.

Local builds read the committed docs/releases.json snapshot. Publishing refreshes it in the generated site from GitHub Releases, without modifying source files. releases.js checks for newer published releases in the browser; a failed or rate-limited GitHub request keeps the working static snapshot. The download, version, date, changelog preview and command-line instructions use the same release. Release notes render without executing embedded HTML or unsafe links.

npm run docs:serve      # build and preview at http://127.0.0.1:8765
npm run docs:review     # check every generated internal link, naming and long references
npm run docs:deploy -- --remote https://github.com/edihasaj/gatefox.git          # dry run
npm run docs:deploy -- --remote https://github.com/edihasaj/gatefox.git --push   # publish

The deploy script builds into a temporary folder under /tmp, adds CNAME (gatefox.dev) and .nojekyll, commits the result as a fresh gh-pages branch and, only with --push, force-pushes that branch. The branch holds generated files only. It adds no Actions workflow, so the CI cost policy is unchanged; GitHub serves a branch-based Pages site of a public repository at no cost.

Search and sharing

Every site update includes a naming and navigation review. docs:review checks all generated pages, local assets and section links before publication. It rejects stale product headings and reports legacy-name mentions and references over 500 lines for human review. Compatibility paths, provider identifiers and historical release names remain literal; visible current branding is GateFox. The publish command runs the same checks and refuses broken destinations.

Long operational pages are split by task, with short overview pages retaining their original section anchors. Every document shows an estimated reading time; mobile readers also get an expandable On this page menu. Keep those original anchors when moving content so existing links continue to work.

Every page gets a title, description, canonical URL, robots with max-image-preview:large, Open Graph and Twitter tags with its own 1200x630 image, and JSON-LD (SoftwareApplication on the guide, TechArticle and BreadcrumbList on doc pages). The build also writes robots.txt, sitemap.xml (every page with its image) and site.webmanifest; the 404 page is noindex. The guide's head is replaced at build time, so edit its description in guideSeo, not in docs/index.html.

Share images live in docs/assets/og/<page>.jpg. After adding a page or changing a title or summary, run node scripts/render-og-images.mjs (needs abx) and commit the images. The template is scripts/og/template.html.

The deploy adds the shared IndexNow key file (/<key>.txt) from COMPASS_INDEXNOW_KEY or ~/.config/compass/search-provider-credentials.json; the key is never committed to the source. Bing ownership uses the account-wide msvalidate.01 tag; Google ownership uses a DNS TXT record in the gatefox.dev zone. A publish with --push then sends the pages whose HTML changed (compared with the published gh-pages branch) to IndexNow; a failed notification is reported in the output but does not undo the publish.

Registered on 8 November 2026: Google Search Console domain property sc-domain:gatefox.dev (owner: the Compass service account; sitemap processed with no errors), Bing Webmaster Tools (verified; sitemap and all 58 URLs submitted; DuckDuckGo follows Bing), IndexNow (58 URLs accepted) and Brave (home page submitted). Lighthouse scores 100 for performance, accessibility, best practices and SEO on the guide, All docs and doc pages.

Hosting

The site is served by GitHub Pages from the gh-pages branch of edihasaj/gatefox, with custom domain gatefox.dev and HTTPS enforced. The Cloudflare zone gatefox.dev (account "Edi") holds two DNS-only records, set up on 8 November 2026 through the dashboard's BIND import, because the Wrangler login cannot edit DNS:

Name Type Content Proxy
gatefox.dev CNAME (flattened at the apex) edihasaj.github.io DNS only
www.gatefox.dev CNAME edihasaj.github.io DNS only

Keep both records unproxied; GitHub issues the certificate only when it sees its own addresses. Every .dev name is HTTPS-only in browsers, so the site opens there only once that certificate exists.

Verify a publish with:

curl -fsSI https://gatefox.dev/
curl -fsS https://gatefox.dev/reference.html | grep -o '<title>[^<]*'
gh api repos/edihasaj/gatefox/pages -q '{status: .status, https: .https_enforced, cname: .cname}'
